after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+7y=4 \\ 6x+42y=24.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 4 \\ 6 & 42 & -24\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 4 \\ 6 & 42 & 24\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-6){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+7y=4 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+7y=4.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=4-7y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=4-7y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4-7y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+7y=4 \\ 6x+42y=24.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 4 \\ 6 & 42 & -24\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 4 \\ 6 & 42 & 24\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-6){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+7y=4 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+7y=4.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=4-7y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=4-7y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4-7y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Apply R₁ ← R₁/4 to obtain [1, −4, 2]. Then R₂ ← R₂ + 3R₁ gives [0, 0, 0]. The resulting row echelon form is option b.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & -16 & 8 \\ -3 & 12 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -16 & 8 \\ -3 & 12 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 \\ -3 & 12 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & -16 & 8 \\ -3 & 12 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -16 & 8 \\ -3 & 12 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 \\ -3 & 12 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 6 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 6 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 6 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 6 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 6 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 6 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-6y=10 \\ -x+3y=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & 10 \\ -1 & 3 & -5\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & 10 \\ -1 & 3 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 \\ -1 & 3 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-3y=5 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-3y=5.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=5+3y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5+3y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5+3y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-6y=10 \\ -x+3y=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & 10 \\ -1 & 3 & -5\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & 10 \\ -1 & 3 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 \\ -1 & 3 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-3y=5 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-3y=5.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=5+3y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5+3y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5+3y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2x+8y=4 \\ -3x+12y=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 8 & 4 \\ -3 & 10 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 8 & 4 \\ -3 & 12 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -2 \\ -3 & 12 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-4y=-2 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-4y=-2.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=4y-2,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=4y-2 \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4y-2 \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2x+8y=4 \\ -3x+12y=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 8 & 4 \\ -3 & 10 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 8 & 4 \\ -3 & 12 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -2 \\ -3 & 12 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-4y=-2 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-4y=-2.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=4y-2,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=4y-2 \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4y-2 \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
